html:
SMTO-CFG-0063 — A Model time limit is outside the allowed range

GUID: 53bdbf6d-82ab-4e07-914d-65c1937d4433
Slug: model-timeout-setting-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • One of the Model's time limits, such as how long SMTO waits for a reply, is set outside the range SMTO allows. SMTO stopped before sending the request to the Model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which time limit SMTO rejected, for example the request timeout or the no-output timeout. Each limit has its own range, so you only need to change the one named.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and expand Limits and recovery for the Model you use. That is where the Model's time limits are saved.
  3. Fix only the named limit: Request timeout 1–1,800 seconds; No-output, Recovery or Capability selection timeout 30–1,800; Recovery deadline 0 or 30–86,400. Then save. Changing one limit doesn't change the others, so leave the rest as they are.
  4. Start a new task. If the error came from continuing an older task, start a new task instead of continuing it. A task keeps the time limits it started with, so only new tasks use your corrected value.

What success looks like

  • A new task gets a reply from the Model without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't raise the Output allowance, the Context ceiling or task time limits to get past this error; they are different limits.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • NativeToolCallLLMClient rejected a model timing value outside its per-field range (request 1–1800 s; no-output, constrained-recovery and capability-selection 30–1800 s; recovery deadline 0 or 30–86400 s), taken from current settings or a resumed run's saved profile.

What this means

  • Model request timeout accepts 1–1,800 seconds. Generation and recovery inactivity allowances and capability-selection timeout accept 30–1,800 seconds. The optional total recovery deadline accepts 0/Off or 30–86,400 seconds. Invalid current or saved values are rejected before inference.

Why this can happen

  • A configured or saved timeout is outside the range accepted for that field.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact timeout field and whether it came from current defaults or a saved profile; changing one does not change the others.

How to fix it

  • Identify the field named in the message and correct only that field in the Model routing profile (Limits and recovery) or in llm_timeout_seconds, llm_no_actionable_output_timeout_seconds, llm_constrained_recovery_timeout_seconds, llm_capability_selection_timeout_seconds or llm_recovery_deadline_seconds (config.yaml llm.* or the AOR_LLM_* environment variables). If the value came from a resumed run's saved profile (prepare_run), that run's settings are fixed; start a new task instead of editing the saved run.
  • Correct the named field: request timeout 1–1,800 seconds; inactivity or capability-selection timeout 30–1,800 seconds; total recovery deadline 0/Off or 30–86,400 seconds. These settings have separate purposes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The named timing setting validates and the request uses the intended saved policy.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
